0.1.n: A humble term for your own company, typically used when speaking to outsiders.

0.3.n: Marks 弊社 as the term being explained.

0.4.n: 私 is a neutral, polite way to refer to yourself.

0.5.n: Links 私 to 会社, making it the speaker’s company.

0.6.n: This first 会社 gives the basic definition of 弊社.

0.8.n: Refers to the speaker as the person working at the company.

0.9.n: Marks 私 as the person doing the working.

0.10.n: 働く becomes 働いている to describe ongoing employment, not necessarily working at this exact moment.

0.11.n: 私が働いている comes before this noun to specify which company.

0.12.n: Politely ends the explanation of what 弊社 means.

1.0.n: Introduces a sample sentence showing how to use 弊社.

1.2.n: The speaker humbly refers to their own company in this business example.

1.3.n: Connects 弊社 with 商品 to show whose products they are.

1.4.n: Japanese nouns do not mark singular or plural; this can refer to one product or several.

1.5.n: Makes 弊社の商品 the topic of the example statement.

1.7.n: Politely finishes the example; the description before it is left as a placeholder.

1.9.n: Presents the quotation as one example among others, leading into the next line.

2.1.n: Uses a humble business term for the company the speaker belongs to.

2.2.n: Marks the company as the setting where the activity takes place.

2.3.n: Added after で, it makes the company setting the topic.

2.5.n: Marks the omitted activity as what the company carries out.

2.6.n: 行う becomes 行っております, a humble, polite version of 行っている describing ongoing or regular activity.

3.1.n: A respectful term for the listener’s company, mainly used in speech.

3.3.n: Marks 御社 as the term being defined.

3.4.n: Identifies the listener in this definition; direct あなた is often avoided in actual business conversation.

3.5.n: Links あなた to 会社 to indicate the company associated with the listener.

3.6.n: Together with あなたの, it explains whose company 御社 refers to.

4.0.n: Introduces a sample use of 御社 in a business sentence.

4.2.n: Sets the time of the visit and needs no に here.

4.3.n: Respectfully refers to the company of the person being addressed.

4.4.n: Marks 御社 as the destination of the visit.

4.5.n: The polite form of 伺う, a humble verb that lowers the speaker’s action to show respect.

0.lit: 弊社, as for, my company—the company where I work—is.
0.tip: 弊社 humbly refers to your own company when addressing people outside it.

1.lit: For example, our company’s products are …, or things like that,
1.tip: とか after a quotation signals that it is one example, not an exhaustive list.

2.lit: At our company, as for, we carry out … .
2.tip: 行っております is a humble, polite way to describe what your company does.

3.lit: 御社, as for, your company is.
3.tip: 御社 respectfully refers to the listener’s company and is mainly used in spoken business Japanese.

4.lit: For example, tomorrow, to your company, I will humbly visit.
4.tip: 伺います shows respect by describing your own visit humbly.
